Goyal Projects India as Future Major Exporter to China and ASEAN Amid Evolving Bilateral Trade

30 Oct 2026, 03:19 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.business-standard.com

Image: Business Standard — Creative Commons

Key takeaways Overview of Trade Outlook and Ministerial Remarks Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated on Tuesday that India is open to Chinese suppliers assisting in fulfilling the nation's rising import demands, provided that transactions adhere to fair trade pr

Overview of Trade Outlook and Ministerial Remarks

Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated on Tuesday that India is open to Chinese suppliers assisting in fulfilling the nation's rising import demands, provided that transactions adhere to fair trade practices. Speaking during a two-day official visit, Goyal expressed optimism that India will establish itself as a prominent exporter of goods and services to China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region in the coming years.

Goyal noted that he had previously held discussions with his Chinese counterpart both in Yaounde, Cameroon, and in New Delhi during the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. He emphasized that while India supports open trade and welcomes necessary intermediate goods and raw materials from Chinese suppliers, the country will rely on established legal and judicial processes to address any instances of unfair pricing or lack of fair play.

Bilateral Trade Figures and Economic Context

Recent data released by the commerce ministry highlights the scale of economic exchange between India and China. During the April-September period of the current fiscal year, bilateral trade grew by approximately 29 percent, reaching $91.76 billion compared to $71.24 billion during the same period in 2025-26. This increase positioned Beijing as India's largest trading partner in the first half of the fiscal year.

This upward trajectory follows broader trade growth recorded in previous financial terms. Bilateral trade between the two nations increased by 7.9 percent to $127.7 billion in 2025-26, up from $118.39 billion in 2024-25. However, trade deficits remain a persistent challenge. India's imports from China grew to $131.62 billion in 2025-26, while exports stood at $19.47 billion, widening the trade deficit to $99.19 billion from $85 billion the previous year.

Diplomatic Background and Border Stance

Goyal's remarks follow recent diplomatic engagements aimed at repairing bilateral relations, which experienced significant strain following the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes and the subsequent military standoff in eastern Ladakh. Ties began to see a gradual thaw after Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in Kazan, Russia, in October 2024.

During a subsequent meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi last month, Prime Minister Modi reiterated that peace and tranquillity along the frontier remain an essential foundation for the development of bilateral relations. Despite these diplomatic steps, economic caution remains, highlighted by tightened foreign direct investment (FDI) policies for countries sharing land borders with India.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

Readers monitoring international trade dynamics can evaluate current developments through several established parameters:

  • Confirmed Elements: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's public statements regarding open trade policies, the legal recourse for unfair pricing, recent bilateral trade statistics for April-September, and ongoing diplomatic dialogue following high-level leader meetings.
  • Unknowns and Uncertainties: The precise timeline for realizing expanded export markets in China and ASEAN, the long-term impact of China's new export controls on machinery such as tunnel boring machines (TBMs) on Indian infrastructure projects, and the ultimate resolution of the broader trade deficit.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review official statements, policy announcements, and periodic trade data releases directly through the Business Standard Report and official publications from India's Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
